description: This policy evaluation and appraisal by the Virginia legislature's audit commission, released on 9 December 2024, reviewed the world's largest concentration of data centres. It found that about 340 data-centre buildings needed some 5 GW of generating capacity and that demand could double within 15 years, making it hard to build enough generation and transmission; that the industry supports about 74,000 jobs, $5.5 billion of labour income and $9.1 billion of annual GDP in Virginia, much of it during construction; and that 80 per cent of the industry sits in Loudoun, Prince William and Fairfax counties, with Loudoun alone about half. It weighed the costs and benefits of the state sales and use tax exemption for data-centre equipment, local land-use powers, noise and water issues, and effects on household electricity bills, and made recommendations and policy options for the 2025 legislative session. Coverage: Virginia, with forecasts to about 2040. Format and access: free full report, summary and briefing slides on the JLARC website, with supporting consultant studies. Caveats: energy forecasts depend on scenarios of industry growth; economic estimates use input-output modelling. Simulation uses: capacity planning of grids and generation for data-centre growth, scenario inputs for load forecasts, and appraisal of incentives and siting policy. Related records: the NERC incident review of the July 2024 load loss concerns the same cluster, EPRI data-centre load projections give national scenarios, and Ireland's grid connection policy is a contrasting regulatory response.
